title: Pinning cache TTL, eviction and subpoena handling notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note capturing recommended TTLs and eviction behavior for prefix/KV caches and transient edge caches when tenants are region-pinned, plus operational guidance for handling legal holds/subpoenas that require retaining or freezing pinned data. Intended to be pragmatic: short, operator-friendly, and designed for iteration during the next residency sprint.

Scope:
- Applies to: prefix/KV cache entries used by inference serving (model KV caches that control where request artifacts are anchored), per-tenant region pin metadata, and transient HTTP edge caches that may store non-sensitive request/response artifacts.
- Does NOT cover long-term audit archives stored in cold object storage (S3/nearline). Those retention policies remain governed by contracts/legal.

TL;DR recommendations (high level):
- Per-tenant pin metadata TTL: 7 days by default, touch-on-read. Operator bump to 30d for customers with manual migration windows.
- Regional edge cache TTL (non-sensitive artifacts): 1 hour default, max 24h. Serve shorter TTLs when telemetry indicates churn.
- KV cache for model state (inference KV cache): eviction governed by LRU + pin-affinity mark; do not evict pinned tenant keys unless forced by emergency operator command.
- Legal hold behavior: a legal_hold flag on tenant metadata => immediate freeze of eviction and start legal_hold retention timer. Legal hold overrides TTLs until explicit release by Legal.

Assumptions and rationale:
- Most region pin changes are deliberate and relatively rare; short TTL on pin metadata lets us correct accidental pins quickly but still converge.
- Long-lived pin metadata causes unnecessary capacity reservation across regions; default 7d is compromise between operational stability and capacity efficiency.
- Legal holds are infrequent but high-risk; must be explicit and auditable. Freezing eviction reduces risk of data loss during discovery/subpoena.

Detailed recommended values and behavior:
1) Tenant pin metadata (central control plane)
   - Default TTL: 7d (604800s).
   - Touch-on-read semantics: read operations extend TTL by +2d up to a configurable max (30d). This prevents churn for active tenants without permanent reservation.
   - Manual pin extension: sales/CS/SEs can request 30d extension with a ticket (ENG-2145 template).
   - Immediate operator override: ops can set ttl=indefinite (represented as "legal_hold" or "pin_locked") in emergencies.

2) Edge transient caches (CDN/region edge nodes)
   - Non-sensitive artifacts (logo assets, model prompts templates): default TTL 3600s, maximum 86400s.
   - Sensitive artifacts (user content, PII): never cached at edge by default; explicit customer opt-in required with explicit encryption-at-rest keys.
   - Eviction trigger: TTL expiry or explicit pin-change event. On pin-change for a tenant, invalidate edge caches with tenant-tag header within 30s via region broadcast.

3) Serving KV caches (model KV cache)
   - Default eviction policy: LRU with pin-affinity boosting. When a tenant is pinned to RegionA, mark keys created by that tenant as "pin-affinity:RegionA". Evict these only when memory pressure is severe AND no legal_hold present.
   - Emergency eviction: ops command "force-evict --tenant T --region R --confirm" required; this logs an auditable event.

4) Legal holds and subpoenas
   - Legal hold flag semantics: setting legal_hold=true on tenant metadata =>
       * Freeze all automated eviction for that tenant across caching layers.
       * Start legal_hold_audit record: who set it, timestamp, reason, Confluence/Jira id for case.
       * Notify oncall and SRE channel.
   - Persistence: legal hold persists until release by Legal. Release requires two approvers (legal + product ops).
   - Telemetry: legal_hold events must emit metrics (legal_hold.active_count, legal_hold.duration_seconds) and be included in daily compliance report.

Operator playbook (quick runbook):
- Scenario: customer requests urgent pin extension for a migration window
  1) Confirm request via ticket and customer contract (link)
  2) Set tenant.pin_ttl=30d via control plane UI or CLI and annotate ticket id
  3) Emit audit event and notify CS + SRE channel

- Scenario: customer served with subpoena requiring data preservation
  1) Legal triages -> creates Jira case and sets legal_hold flag in control plane with reference to Jira case id
  2) System freezes eviction; SRE runs snapshot script to persist hot KV to escrow bucket (encrypted) and verifies checksum
  3) Daily status note until release

Eviction notification & audit:
- Any automatic eviction that affects pinned tenants must create an audit entry with fields: tenant_id, keys_affected, reason, operator_override (if any). These entries should be centralized and queryable by CS/legal.
- Notifications: send webhook to customer contacts on planned bulk eviction that may impact performance (during maintenance).

Telemetry and monitoring:
- Metrics to emit:
  - tenant_pin.ttl_seconds (histogram)
  - tenant_pin.touch_count (counter)
  - edge_cache.invalidate_count (counter by region)
  - legal_hold.active_count (gauge)
  - eviction.events (counter, labelled by tenant, cause)
- Dashboards: create "Residency: Pin & Cache Health" with top 10 tenants by pin TTL, number of legal holds, and eviction rate by region.

Testing & rollout plan:
- Step 0: Unit tests for TTL touch semantics and legal_hold override behavior.
- Step 1: Canary in staging with 10 synthetic tenants mimicking migrations. Validate touch-on-read and expiration behavior.
- Step 2: Beta rollout to 5 low-risk customers with opt-in. Monitor eviction.events and ops tickets.
- Step 3: Default rollout with feature flag; monitor for churn and customer complaints for 2 weeks before disabling flag.

Open questions / risks:
- Should default TTL be shorter (48h) for dev/test tenants to reduce regional idle capacity? (pro: cost, con: accidental pin rollbacks)
- Interaction with dedicated/reserved pools: do we treat reserved-capacity tenants as "pinned-permanent" by default? Need contract-driven mapping.
- Legal hold scale: if many holds appear simultaneously, we may run out of local KV capacity — need escalation and escrow automation.

Action items before next sync (owners):
- (Avery) Draft CLI UX for pin extension and legal_hold flags (due 2025-11-14)
- (Priya) Add metrics to telemetry plan and stub dashboards (due 2025-11-18)
- (Ethan) Create the canary test harness for touch-on-read and eviction flows (due 2025-11-21)
- (Legal) Provide template for legal_hold justification that can be pasted into audit records (requested)

Notes to self / loose thoughts (brainstorm-y):
- Consider a soft-fallback: when a pin TTL expires we keep a "stale-resident" marker for 48h to reduce churn thrash. Will simulate.
- Might be useful to add a "pin-intent" enum: {temporary, migration-window, long-term, legal_hold} for clearer UI and billing implications.

References:
- See ENG-2145 (pin extension workflow)
- Confluence: Residency: region-pin-spec (linked above)
- PR: pinning-service/#542 contains recent refactor of touch-on-read logic

Appendix: sample audit note (copy/paste)
- event_type: pin_ttl_override
- tenant: ACME-Corp-123
- actor: maria.gonzalez@redwood.ai
- reason: customer migration window approved by sales (ticket CS-4592)
- previous_ttl: 7d
- new_ttl: 30d
- ticket: CS-4592
- timestamp: 2025-11-10T15:32:04Z

----
End of working note. This doc is intentionally lightweight; will expand and formalize into a playbook doc once we validate canary results.
